name: Immunoglobulin-mediated Membranoproliferative Glomerulonephritis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on histopathology and immunofluorescence

criteria.description: Light microscopy showing mesangial hypercellularity and double-contour glomerular basement membrane (GBM) thickening
Presence of immunoglobulin deposits (IgG, IgM, and/or IgA) and complement components (C3) in glomeruli
Evidence of nephritic or nephrotic syndrome with proteinuria and hematuria
Exclusion of other causes of MPGN such as complement-mediated or infection-related MPGN

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological evidence of membranoproliferative pattern with immunoglobulin deposits plus clinical evidence of glomerulonephritis, excluding other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Renal biopsy with immunofluorescence is essential for diagnosis.

laboratory: Proteinuria often in nephrotic range (>3.5 g/day)
Microscopic hematuria with dysmorphic red blood cells
Low serum complement levels (C3 and C4) in some cases
Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (BUN)
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or increased kidney size in early disease
No specific imaging findings diagnostic for MPGN
other: Renal biopsy demonstrating membranoproliferative pattern with immunoglobulin and complement deposits
Electron microscopy showing subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of immunoglobulin deposits on immunofluorescence
Associated with complement regulatory protein mutations
History of recent or ongoing infection (e.g., hepatitis C, endocarditis)
Resolution of glomerulonephritis with treatment of infection

redFlags: Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with declining renal function
Nephrotic syndrome with severe hypoalbuminemia and edema
Uncontrolled hypertension leading to cardiovascular complications
